A.name: Mayor Jared Gray
A.basis: conducts both sessions — opens the work session ('we'll go ahead and get started right on 4 o'clock'), calls the policy session to order at 7:05, names each member in every roll call, and adjourns at 9:41; addressed as 'Mayor' throughout ('Mayor, can you go back to the one that shows…', 'All right, Mayor, if you'll entertain a motion') and by name at the end, when Councilmember Whiting says 'if they don't, Jared, Mayor Gray, we got this recorded'

B.name: Councilmember Brett Wright
B.basis: the mayor restates his Brylee Farms question as 'I think what Councilmember Wright's asking is…' immediately after this speaker asks it, and Councilmember Whiting answers 'I'm along the lines of what Council Member Wright's asking'; moves the Transportation Master Plan ordinance, which the mayor records as 'a motion by Councilmember Wright'; thanks 'Steve' for the Healthy Utah work and asks LBiSat the sight-line questions the mayor and Huish then build on. The roll call once renders his name 'Councilmember Wrobel-Wright.' A few short lines under this letter are not his — the diarizer folds in the recorder calling 'Charlotte Dukos' off the comment cards, and the LBiSat president's 'I'm the president of our company here'

C.name: Towns at Brylee Farms developer's representative (name not on the record)
C.basis: presents item 1.A from the applicant's side — 'Last week at the City Council meeting, you approved the first amendment to the development agreement… I used to be on a planning commission' — and carries the whole garage exchange (the 24-foot-deep, 496-square-foot garage, the 20.08-foot width, the 520-square-foot basement, the 378 required vs 386 provided stalls). The mayor's opening line invites 'Greg' up, which is likely him, but when the mayor asks 'Could you state your name for the record?' it is Element Homes' Taylor Keyes who answers, so his name is never recorded

D.name: Corey Wofford (President, LBiSat)
D.basis: gives the LBiSat presentation — 'Last time I was able to talk to the city council was in 2020… We are a satellite communications company, and we moved from South Jordan down here' — explains the 10-degree look angle and the GEO/LEO contracts, introduces his colleague ('This is Rusty Lake,' the recording's rendering of Rusty Layton), and states 'my name is Corey Wofford' before the garage comparison. The transcript writes the company as 'LVISAT'

E.name: Councilmember Craig Whiting
E.basis: moves the closed session, the Youth Council mayor, the seventeen Youth Council members, and the substitute Scenic Mountain motion, each recorded by the mayor as 'a motion by Councilmember Whiting'; says 'I'm along the lines of what Council Member Wright's asking' on the garages and 'I'm comfortable with the staff providing their recommendations' on the project list; Huish sums up the same item with 'I would agree with Brett and Craig'

F.name: Taylor Keyes (Element Homes)
F.basis: answers the mayor's 'Could you state your name for the record?' with 'Taylor Keyes with Element Homes on the sales part of it,' then works through which Brylee Farms buildings are still unpoured and closes with 'I think we can take that feedback and get back with the team.' Four scattered one-liners under this letter belong to others — a roll-call prompt, a 'Second,' and the motion to adjourn the mayor attributes to Councilmember Wood

G.name: Councilmember Zac Huish
G.basis: frames the LBiSat item as 'a property rights issue' and 'I'm not even sure as a council how we can restrict or zone the airspace above their property'; pushes to keep some of the Ranches Parkway median, which the mayor recaps as 'Councilmember Herwish was saying he wanted to leave some of the median, and Councilmember Wright said he wanted to take them out'; reports on the Community Services Board at the end. The recording spells his surname 'Hewish,' 'Herwish,' 'Herish,' and once 'Hughes'

H.name: Melissa Powers (resident, Evans Ranch)
H.basis: speaks after the recorder reads her name off the comment cards — 'Good evening, Mayor Gray and members of the City Council. My name is Melissa Powers. I live in Evans Ranch neighborhood, which butts up right against Silver Lake' — in support of the Silver Lake Parkway changes. Her other five turns under this letter are one- and two-word fragments the diarizer could not place, not her

I.name: Councilmember Rich Wood
I.basis: presses the Brylee Farms developer on garage width rather than depth, and the developer answers 'I heard Councilmember Wood say that he was less concerned about that' about parking; asks LBiSat 'why 10 acres? Why not 50?'; takes the middle position on the medians — 'I'm going to hit somewhere in the middle on this one. I agree with what you're saying, Brett' — and moves the evening closed session, recorded as 'a motion by Councilmember Wood'

J.name: Councilmember Melissa Clark
J.basis: suggests the Brylee Farms overflow parking the mayor then sums up, and asks that the project list flag anything 'at a critical state, like we're at capacity for a wastewater treatment plant'; after her block grant question the mayor notes for the record 'when Melissa asked the question that Charlotte Duco shook her head no'; moves the consent agenda, recorded as 'a motion by Councilmember Clark'; closes with the UTA on-demand open house

K.name: David Salazar (Assistant City Engineer)
K.basis: presents item 16.B after the mayor says 'I know David Salazar has done a lot of work on this, and we'll turn it to you' — 'the purpose of today's item is that we are bringing the Transportation Master Plan back' — and carries the whole road discussion: the Silver Lake signal, the Stonebridge landscaping example, the roundabout removal at Eagle Mountain Boulevard, and the recurring meeting he is setting up with the school district. A resident also says 'I spoke to David earlier tonight.' The scattered short lines under this letter during the work session are not his, and the legislative-priorities turn ('those are the 2 areas… at the state level') is John Magnus

L.name: Ben Reeves (City Manager)
L.basis: delivers the consolidated project list, the longest presentation of the day — 'we can do anything, but not everything. As soon as we try, that's when we fail, because we're spread too thin' — and answers 'We do' when the mayor asks 'Mr. Reeves, do we have any public information items?' before reading the Summer Splash and Truth in Taxation announcements. This letter is the day's catch-all and carries at least four other voices: John Magnus on the legislative list ('I still owe you the list for the state legislative'), Evan flagging the block grant noticing error, City Attorney Marcus on whether the general plan amendment needs its own motion ('So Marcus, are you good with one motion or do you want 2?'), the block grant presenter's thank-you, and Miss Eagle Mountain's Teen, 'My name is Brighton Hawes'

M.name: Steve Mumford (Community Services)
M.basis: presents the Healthy Utah Community designation after the mayor says 'Steve is gonna lead this,' opening 'Thank you, Mayor'; walks the nine implemented strategies and the county health data, and Councilmember Wright replies 'Steve, there's actually a woman that has been at the farmers market that is promoting the Special Olympics.' The transcript gives only his first name; the surname follows the earlier meetings, where Steve Mumford is the staff member working with the Community Services Board

N.name: Brad (Public Works)
N.basis: the mayor turns to him by first name — 'but Brad, we already have some places, right' — for the failed community garden near Pioneer Park, and again during LBiSat, 'there is a question over here, Brad'; gives the grade difference to the satellite site and the warning that a 250-foot buffer 'basically takes in almost our whole buildable footprint for our treatment plant facility upgrade.' No surname is spoken on the record

O.name: Brandon Larsen (Community Development Director)
O.basis: Councilmember Wood asks 'Do you know what the height of the building is, Brandon?' and this speaker answers; walks the zoning maps, the QTS retention basin 320 feet off the shared line, and the RTI overlay, offers LBiSat a contact at the data center, and is thanked as 'Thanks, Brandon.' He also picks up the Scenic Mountain rezoning with 'I'm going to take this one' when the mayor cannot find Robert Hobbs. The transcript gives only 'Brandon'; the surname follows the earlier meetings

P.name: Quinn Lindy (principal, the new high school)
P.basis: called up off the comment cards and opens 'Mayor and Council, my name is Quinn Lindy. I am the principal of the new high school that was opening in Saratoga Springs'; gives the roughly 900-students-per-access-point figure and insists 'this is not an Eagle Mountain High School. It will not be a Saratoga Springs High School. I live in Eagle Mountain and I have since 2013.' Councilmember Wright then refers to 'the principal of the new high school.' The spelling of the surname is uncertain. His handful of one-word turns earlier in the day are backchannel the diarizer could not place

Q.name: Rusty Layton (LBiSat)
Q.basis: states 'just for the record, Rusty Layton with LVISAT' and handles the technical half of the item — the 7-degree versus 10-degree look angle math, the 85-foot setback, the RF radiation buffer, and the walk-back of the 250-foot figure ('so that takes it down to 210'); the LBiSat president introduces him as 'Rusty' and asks 'Do you have any other insight on that, Rusty?'

R.name: Charlotte Dukos (resident; Community Services Board)
R.basis: the only speaker at the block grant hearing, opening 'All right, Charlotte Dukos. I'm just here to talk about the Community Development Block Grant because I was having a conversation with principal over at Cedar Valley High School'; describes the proposed Eagle Mountain Community Center and asks that capital money be considered. Staff earlier place her on the Community Services Board — 'I started working with our Community Services Board, with Jesse and Charlotte and the board.' The mayor renders her surname 'Charlotte Duco'

S.name: Duncan "DJ" Searcy (resident)
S.basis: the general public comment — 'I'm DJ, more commonly known as Duncan Searcy. I've missed you guys' — on the proposed property tax increase, warning about neighbors living paycheck to paycheck and saying the law-enforcement framing 'rubbed people the wrong way'

T.name: Ben Perez (resident)
T.basis: speaks after the recorder reads 'Ben Perez' off the cards, supporting the master plan change: 'my son attended the ALL program at Silver Lake Elementary last year, and one thing that he was adamant about was that he did not want us' to pick him up in front of the school, and describing near-misses at the roundabout. His one other line under this letter is the mayor's roll call

U.name: Miss Eagle Mountain royalty — Treea Smith and Emmeline Smith
U.basis: covers two of the three young women introduced at item 9.A: Emmeline Smith ('my name is Emmeline Smith and I'm honored to serve this year as Miss Teen Eagle Mountain's first runner-up') and Treea Smith ('my name is Treea Smith, and I'm so, so honored to be able to be crowned Miss Eagle Mountain… This was my 5th year competing'), who also leads the Pledge of Allegiance after the mayor introduces 'our Miss Eagle Mountain 2026.' The third, Brighton Hawes, is folded into the city manager's letter

V.name: Elizabeth McNanny (Resource Consultants, block grant consultant)
V.basis: answers the council's block grant questions — whether a school-attached center 'could possibly qualify' and 'would qualify as a public facility,' that donated labor is fine 'as long as they're qualified contractors,' and that small shifts between buckets are allowed while larger ones need a plan amendment — and closes 'Thank you, Council.' Identified by voice, not by name: this letter was first read as Kiara Poole, because the agenda lists the item as presented by the Affordable Housing Coordinator and the recording renders the surname 'Polee' elsewhere, but nobody says a name here. Comparing the audio against the 21 July work session, where both consultants introduce themselves out loud, matches it to Elizabeth McNanny at 0.92 cosine similarity and to Poole at only 0.21 — on a scale where no two different people in this archive score above 0.64. McNanny gave the block grant presentation on 21 July, so the consultant answering block grant questions here is the more likely of the two in any case. Four turns under this letter are City Recorder Lacie Messerly instead, reading names off the comment cards ('Quinn Lindy.' 'Melissa Powers.' 'Ben Perez.') and noting the Youth Council 'have their oaths of office'
